question: Under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Samhita(BNSS), the period for default bail in minor offences is capped at?
solution:
The correct answer is __**60 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Samhita (BNSS)**, the timeline for default bail in minor offences has been capped at **60 days**.
 
• This period is aligned with the procedural reforms introduced in the BNSS to streamline criminal justice delivery and ensure timely disposal of cases.
 
• **Minor offences** are typically classified as offences punishable with imprisonment of up to three years.
 
• The BNSS aims to modernize and simplify procedural laws, replacing the traditional Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) with updated provisions.
 
• The emphasis on default bail timelines ensures the protection of individual rights and prevents unnecessary detention.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional __**

 
• **BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita): **Replaces the IPC; focuses on defining criminal offenses, introducing new crimes (like organized crime), and updating punishments, including for repeat offenders and offenses against women/children.
 
• **BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita): **Replaces the CrPC; covers the procedural aspects of investigation and trial, streamlining processes, ensuring time limits for stages, and incorporating technology like video recording.
 
• **BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam): **Replaces the Indian Evidence Act; deals with rules of evidence, including digital evidence, DNA, and modern forensic methods.
